assertion_results.text: Epics are generated between Feature and Tasks — at least 2 Epics are created (one per repository) when by-repository grouping is used
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md lines 41-43: 'Strategy: by-repository (from CLAUDE.md Hierarchy Configuration)', 'Epic 1: TC-9006: trustify-backend', 'Epic 2: TC-9006: trustify-ui'. Two Epics are created, one per repository, with by-repository grouping strategy.

assertion_results.text: Each Epic summary follows the format '<feature-key>: <repository-name>' (e.g., 'TC-9006: trustify-backend', 'TC-9006: trustify-ui')
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md lines 42-43: 'Epic 1: TC-9006: trustify-backend' and 'Epic 2: TC-9006: trustify-ui'. Both follow the '<feature-key>: <repository-name>' format exactly.

assertion_results.text: Each task specifies its parent Epic key in the output — tasks targeting trustify-backend are assigned to the backend Epic, tasks targeting trustify-ui are assigned to the frontend Epic
assertion_results.evidence: summary-comment.md documents Epic assignment: 'Epic: TC-9006: trustify-backend (4 tasks)' lists Tasks 1, 2, 3, 8 and 'Epic: TC-9006: trustify-ui (4 tasks)' lists Tasks 4, 5, 6, 7. impact-map.md lines 63-68 confirm: 'Each Task is created with: parent: assigned Epic key (trustify-backend Epic or trustify-ui Epic)'. All backend-repo tasks (1, 2, 3, 8) go to backend Epic; all UI-repo tasks (4, 5, 6, 7) go to UI Epic.

assertion_results.text: The plan documents Incorporates links from the Feature to each Epic (not from Feature to individual Tasks) — evidenced by link decisions in the impact map or task output files
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md lines 71-73 under 'Feature "incorporates" links (Epic-aware)': 'TC-9006 "Incorporates" --> trustify-backend Epic' and 'TC-9006 "Incorporates" --> trustify-ui Epic'. Links are from Feature to Epics only, not to individual Tasks.

assertion_results.text: Task dependency ordering is preserved within and across Epics — backend tasks have lower task numbers than dependent frontend tasks
assertion_results.evidence: Backend tasks: 1, 2, 3 (implementation), 8 (documentation). Frontend tasks: 4, 5, 6, 7. impact-map.md lines 76-85 show: Task 4 (frontend) depends on Tasks 1 and 2 (backend); Task 5 depends on Task 4; Task 6 depends on Task 5; Task 7 depends on Tasks 5 and 6. All backend implementation tasks that frontend depends on (1, 2) have lower numbers than dependent frontend tasks (4-7). Task 8 (doc) depends on all others, correctly ordered last.

assertion_results.text: Each non-documentation, non-testing task file contains all required template sections: Repository, Target Branch, Description, at least one of Files to Modify or Files to Create, Implementation Notes, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements. Documentation tasks (tasks whose filename or description indicates doc-only scope) and testing tasks (tasks whose filename or description indicates cross-cutting testing scope) are exempt from requiring Files to Modify, Files to Create, and Implementation Notes — they must still include Repository, Target Branch, Description, Acceptance Criteria, and Test Requirements
assertion_results.evidence: Non-doc, non-test tasks (1, 2, 4, 5, 6) all contain: Repository, Target Branch, Description, Files to Create, Files to Modify, Implementation Notes, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements. Testing tasks (3: 'remediation-integration-tests', 7: 'dashboard-tests') contain Repository, Target Branch, Description, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements (and also include Files to Create, Files to Modify, Implementation Notes — exceeding the minimum). Documentation task 8 ('remediation-documentation') contains Repository, Target Branch, Description, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements — correctly omits Files to Modify, Files to Create, and Implementation Notes as exempt.

assertion_results.text: The plan documents Epic creation with the level-1 issue type name ('Epic') and parent set to the feature issue key — evidenced by Epic creation parameters in the impact map or output files
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md lines 55-59 under 'Epic additional_fields': 'Each Epic is created with: parent: TC-9006 (the Feature issue)'. The issue type is identified as 'Epic' throughout (section header 'Epic Grouping', 'Epic 1', 'Epic 2', 'Epic additional_fields'). Parent is explicitly set to TC-9006.

assertion_results.text: Every generated task description contains a Repository section with a single repository name (not multiple repos per task)
assertion_results.evidence: All 8 task files have a '## Repository' section with a single value: Tasks 1, 2, 3, 8 have 'trustify-backend'; Tasks 4, 5, 6, 7 have 'trustify-ui'. No task lists multiple repositories.

assertion_results.text: Every generated task description contains Target Branch, Description, Acceptance Criteria, and Test Requirements sections as required by the handoff contract in task-description-template.md
assertion_results.evidence: All 8 task files contain '## Target Branch' (all set to 'main'), '## Description', '## Acceptance Criteria', and '## Test Requirements' sections. Verified in task-1 through task-8 output files.

assertion_results.text: For each task created, a description digest is produced — evidenced by a separate digest file (e.g., task-N-digest.md), a digest entry in the impact map, or a '[sdlc-workflow] Description digest: sha256-md:<64-char-hex>' marker in any output file. The digest must contain a format-tagged SHA-256 hash — exactly 64 lowercase hex characters prefixed by 'sha256-md:' or 'sha256-adf:', not a placeholder, abbreviated value, or example string
assertion_results.evidence: Digest files exist for all 8 tasks (task-1-digest.md through task-8-digest.md). However, every digest file contains the placeholder 'sha256-adf:<64-char-hex-digest>' instead of an actual 64-character hex hash. The note in each file states 'The actual hex digest would be computed from the Jira-persisted description content.' The assertion requires 'exactly 64 lowercase hex characters', 'not a placeholder, abbreviated value, or example string'. The placeholder '<64-char-hex-digest>' fails this requirement.

assertion_results.text: Convention-aware enrichment validates file-type applicability per shared/convention-applicability-rules.md before including a convention — inapplicable conventions are excluded entirely (not listed with 'Not applicable' annotations), and applicable ones include a rationale in the prescribed format ('Applies: task modifies <file> matching the convention's <scope>'), not free-form prose
assertion_results.evidence: All convention references in task Implementation Notes follow the prescribed rationale format. Examples: Task 1: 'Applies: task creates `modules/fundamental/src/remediation/mod.rs` matching the convention's Rust module scope.'; Task 4: 'Applies: task creates `src/hooks/useRemediationSummary.ts` matching the convention's `.ts` file scope.'; Task 5: 'Applies: task modifies `src/routes.tsx` matching the convention's `.tsx` file scope.' No inapplicable conventions are listed with 'Not applicable' annotations. No free-form prose rationales are present. All rationales name a specific file and scope.

assertion_results.text: When the Feature issue has a priority set (not 'Undefined'), the plan documents that the Feature's priority is inherited by created tasks — evidenced by priority field values in the impact map, task creation log, or task description files. When the Feature's priority is 'Undefined', the plan documents that priority inheritance is skipped (not propagated as null or 'Undefined')
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md line 49: 'priority: {"name": "Major"} (inherited from Feature; Feature priority is "Major", not "Undefined")'. Lines 63-68 confirm each Task is created with 'priority: {"name": "Major"}'. summary-comment.md line 46: 'Priority: Major (propagated from Feature TC-9006 to all Epics and Tasks)'. Priority is Major (not Undefined), and it is documented as inherited.

assertion_results.text: When the Feature issue has a non-empty fixVersions array and the fixVersion scope config (from ### Jira Field Defaults in CLAUDE.md) is 'task' or 'both' (or absent, defaulting to 'both'), the plan documents that fixVersions are inherited by created tasks — evidenced by fixVersion values in the impact map, task creation log, or task description files. When fixVersion scope is 'feature' or the Feature has no fixVersions, the plan documents that fixVersion inheritance is skipped
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md line 50: 'fixVersions: [{"name": "RHTPA 1.5.0"}] (inherited from Feature; no `fixVersion scope` setting in Jira Field Defaults, so defaults to "both" -- propagated to tasks)'. Lines 67-68 confirm Tasks are created with 'fixVersions: [{"name": "RHTPA 1.5.0"}]'. summary-comment.md line 47: 'fixVersions: RHTPA 1.5.0 (propagated from Feature TC-9006 to all Epics and Tasks; no `fixVersion scope` setting in Jira Field Defaults, defaulting to "both")'. fixVersion scope is absent, correctly defaults to 'both', and fixVersions are propagated.

assertion_results.text: A summary of inherited field propagation is produced — evidenced by a summary-comment.md file in the outputs directory, or a summary section in the impact map that includes the inherited priority and fixVersion values propagated to tasks, or states they were omitted and why
assertion_results.evidence: summary-comment.md exists in the outputs directory and contains '### Inherited Field Values' section (lines 45-47): 'Priority: Major (propagated from Feature TC-9006 to all Epics and Tasks)' and 'fixVersions: RHTPA 1.5.0 (propagated from Feature TC-9006 to all Epics and Tasks; no `fixVersion scope` setting in Jira Field Defaults, defaulting to "both")'. Additionally, impact-map.md has a full 'Jira Field Propagation (additional_fields)' section (lines 46-68) documenting the same.
